title: After a second claim's root ends, re-naming the first claim's root stays 'bound root differs' turn after turn: same-generation naming does not update the session's bound root
outcome: A session returning to a held claim, whose root it names again, gets a confirmed opening on its next turn, or a notice whose remedy actually works; it does not stay unconfirmed with evidence withheld after following the notice.
acceptance: A deterministic regression starts with two held claims and separately named roots, ends the later claim, returns to the first claim, names its already selected root again, and opens the next turn with that first claim's exact selected root and generation confirmed; the regression fails on the original source and passes with the fix.

A genuinely different bound root or stale generation remains unconfirmed. Re-naming does not bypass current claim/store/run identity, unresolved authority transitions, durability or next-turn source-root activation, and creates no false evidence for the naming turn.

The exact candidate passes focused regression and negative-control tests, has the required independent review pair with no outstanding Medium-or-higher finding, and passes the applicable full gate before landing.
